_meta.indication: For the treatment of patients with locally recurrent or metastatic, progressive, radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer

pivotal_trials.population: Patients with locally recurrent or metastatic radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer with radiographic evidence of disease progression within 12 months prior to randomization
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) as the primary objective; key secondary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR) and overall survival (OS)
pivotal_trials.n: 392 patients randomized (261 to lenvatinib, 131 to placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 18.3 months for lenvatinib vs 3.6 months for placebo; HR 0.21 (95% CI 0.16, 0.28), p<0.001; ORR 65% vs 2%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥30%) are hypertension, fatigue, diarrhea, arthralgia/myalgia, decreased appetite, weight decreased, nausea, stomatitis, headache, vomiting, proteinuria, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, abdominal pain, and dysphonia. In Study 1 hypertension was reported in 73% of LENVIMA-treated patients vs 16% of placebo (Grade 3 hypertension 44% vs 4%); hemorrhagic events in 35% vs 18%.
target_moa: Lenvatinib is a kinase inhibitor (anti-VEGFR/tyrosine kinase inhibitor)

boxed_warning.content: No Boxed Warning; none proposed by Eisai and FDA did not require a Boxed Warning

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee because the safety profile was acceptable and the Study 303 trial design was acceptable to demonstrate clinical benefit

description.text: Added accelerated approval of lenvatinib in combination with pembrolizumab for advanced endometrial carcinoma (not MSI-H/dMMR) with progression after prior systemic therapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the following indication: LENVIMA®, in combination with pembrolizumab, is indicated for the treatment of patients with advanced endometrial carcinoma that is not microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or mismatch repair deficient (dMMR), who have disease progression following prior systemic therapy and are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in the confirmatory trial.

summary.text: LENVIMA received a priority review based on unmet medical need in patients with prior anti-VEGF/VEGFR therapy and had orphan drug designation; it was approved February 13, 2015 on the basis of a single randomized placebo-controlled trial (SELECT) demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in PFS, without accelerated approval.

citations.quote: The NDA was granted priority review status based on the unmet medical need in the subgroup of patients who had received prior anti-VEGF/VEGFR therapy.
Eisai was granted Orphan Drug Designation on December 27, 2012 for lenvatinib for the “treatment of follicular, medullary, anaplastic, and metastatic or locally advanced papillary thyroid cancer.”
A statistically significant prolongation in PFS was demonstrated in LENVIMA-treated patients compared to those receiving placebo [HR 0.21 (0.16, 0.28), p < 0.001]
This replacement approval letter incorporates the correction of the error. The effective approval date will remain February 13, 2015, the date of the original approval letter.
